Latest official record: ZEC General Notices 1128-1130 of 2023 (30 June 2023) list the party as 'MDC-T' (party lists, National Assembly) and its presidential nominee Mwonzora under 'MDC'.
Drafted 2026-10-20 by automated research; sources as listed.
OTHER 2025-2026 PRESS (leads, not sources): CITE, 24 Mar 2025 (Lulu Brenda Harris, https://cite.org.zw/mwonzora-courts-punishing-mdc-for-opposing-mnangagwas-3rd-term-bid/): calls it 'Movement for Democratic Change (MDC)', Douglas Mwonzora 'MDC leader'; High Court (Justice Hapias Zhou) nullified the MDC's 2022 congress (24 days' notice instead of 30; women's congress not concluded); Mwonzora says the Supreme Court appeal suspends the judgment; Elias Mudzuri named as vice president, Gift Chimanikire leading talks with Mudzuri's group. AllAfrica, 17 Jul 2025: Mudzuri moving to take Harvest House citing a Feb 2025 High Court ruling; national youth chair Albert Chidhakwa says 'President Mwonzora remains the party leader'; Morgen Komichi said to back Mudzuri; party did not take part in the 2023 elections (withdrew after nomination). New Zimbabwe via AllAfrica, 6 Nov 2025 (https://allafrica.com/stories/202511070038.html): armed men in ZANU PF regalia stormed the MDC Bulawayo provincial office after the party opposed the presidential term extension. AllAfrica, 13 Nov 2025 (first-pass lead): youths seized Harvest House. NewsDay, 21 Jan 2026 (metadata only, paywalled, https://newsday.co.zw/local-news/article/200050733/mwonzora-bounces-back-at-harvest-house): Mwonzora 'bounces back at Harvest House' while fighting the ruling that invalidated the 2022 congress.
NAME: the party calls itself Movement for Democratic Change (MDC); '-T'/'Tsvangirai' was the ballot/media label from the 2005 split and ZEC still used 'MDC-T' in 2023, so this is treated as the same party, not a rename. Verifier: consider displaying it as 'Movement for Democratic Change (MDC)'. Not a duplicate of the CCC record.
LEADER left empty: Mwonzora was the party's 2023 presidential nominee (ZEC) and is called leader/president in press, but the leadership is before the courts (High Court ruling on the 2022 congress, appeal pending; VP Mudzuri contests) and no official or party source naming current office-bearers was found.
CONSTITUTION / FOUNDING: the 2014 constitution is the latest read; amendments at the 2020 extraordinary congress or the 2022 congress (press) were not seen. year_founded 1999 is the original MDC launch given in the preamble; the MDC-T faction itself dates from the 2005 split (verifier to choose). REGISTRATION: no statutory register of political parties found for Zimbabwe; parties contest through the nomination court.
MONEY: no party accounts or donor disclosures published. Not shown as a recipient under the Political Parties (Finance) Act [Chapter 2:11] (5% vote threshold); the other ZW records' notes cite press (AllAfrica, 3 Sep 2025) that the 2025 allocation went only to ZANU PF and the CCC.
PARENT GROUP: Socialist International member list (socialistinternational.org/about-us/members/, read 2026-10-20) has no Zimbabwean party. Progressive Alliance participants page (progressive-alliance.info/?p=2813, modified 2023-09-06) lists 'Movement for Democratic Change (MDC Renewal)', which is Biti's 2014 breakaway that became the PDP, not this party; left empty.
CHANNELS: no official website or party social account found; Mwonzora's personal X account @DMwonzora appears in the New Zimbabwe article (personal, not entered).
